item.title: Ni@PdCu Core–Shell Catalyst for Direct H 2 O 2 Synthesis: Strain–Ligand Synergy Revealed by Experiment and DFT
item.description:
Abstract
Direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (DSHP) from H2 and O2 over Pd-based catalysts offers a green alternative to the anthraquinone process, yet its practical application is hindered by the inherent activity-selectivity trade-off of Pd. Herein, we report a Ni@PdCu core–shell catalyst supported on N-doped porous carbon (Ni@PdCu/NPCs) synthesized via a two-step ethylene glycol-assisted reduction strategy, which achieves an exceptional H2O2 selectivity of 95.3%. Systematic characterization by TEM, XRD, XPS, and ICP-OES confirms the successful construction of the Ni@PdCu core–shell architecture with a uniform PdCu alloy shell. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrate that the strain effect, combined with the geometric isolation of Pd sites by Cu alloying, synergistically increases the O2* dissociation barrier from 0.56 to 0.84 eV while decreasing the hydrogenation barrier from 0.88 to 0.60 eV, thereby redirecting the reaction pathway from O–O bond cleavage toward H2O2 formation. This work establishes a synergistic strain-ligand engineering strategy for designing high-performance Pd-based catalysts for DSHP.

item.title: Toxicological Assessment of Some Synthesized Carbazole Derivatives Using Computational Interaction with CYP2D6 and In Vivo Zebrafish Embryonic Model
item.description:
Abstract
Effective management of etiologically complex clinical disorders such as depression usually warrants polypharmacy, a subject of toxicity through drug–drug interactions (DDIs). Metabolism-associated DDI occurs mainly through the irreversible inhibition of the cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes, such as CYP2D6, and this affects several marketed antidepressants. From our previous study, an IBScreen database piperazine-linked carbazole derivative (PCD), STOCK3S-94557, was identified as a putative adjuvating/stand-alone antidepressant, suggestively acting through serotonergic pathways. In this study, two PCD analogues, YF1C and YF3A, were synthesized and characterized using GC-MS, 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy. Their toxicity propensities were studied using in silico interactions with the CYP2D6 enzyme and experimental validation in an in vivo zebrafish embryonic toxicity model. The characterization techniques successfully elucidated the targeted PCDs with a purity of >98%. In the in vivo zebrafish model, YF1C and YF3A imparted no significant toxicity on the embryos at concentrations between 0.5 and 10.0 mg/L. They supported normal hatching, heartbeat rates, and morphological development, without yolk edema and lordosis, following a 96 h post-fertilization exposure to their solutions. These are similar to the effects of the system water and 0.1% DMSO solution (negative controls), while doxorubicin (DOX, positive control) impacted hatching, heartbeats, and morphology, with eventual 100% toxicity-induced mortality. From molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and ADMET predictions, they demonstrated reversible inhibitory interactions and compatibility with the CYP2D6 enzyme, comparable to reference reversible inhibitors (quinidine and ajmalicine), and interesting drug-like properties, implying low tendencies for DDI events. These findings suggest that YF1C and YF3A possess ideal safety for further study as potential drugs.

item.title: Calcium Alginate/Polyaniline-PSS Core–Shell Particles: Synthesis and Multi-Mechanism Water Vapor Adsorption Behavior
item.description:
Abstract
Core–shell composite particles combining a calcium alginate (Alg-Ca) hydrogel core with a polyaniline/polystyrene sulfonic acid (PANi/PSS) conductive polymer shell were synthesized and evaluated for water vapor adsorption applications. The resulting particles exhibited a well-defined, phase-separated architecture, comprising a highly hydrated, porous hydrogel core encapsulated by a structurally and chemically distinct shell, consistent with successful incorporation of the sulfonated conductive polymer onto the surface of the alginate network. The core and shell regions displayed markedly different thermal decomposition behavior, confirming their compositional distinction and demonstrating that the composite retains thermal stability within the operating range typical of gas-sensing applications. Kinetic analysis of water vapor adsorption as a function of relative humidity (RH, 50–95%) and temperature (25–45 °C) revealed a systematic transition among pseudo-first-order, pseudo-second-order, and Elovich kinetic models. At moderate RH, adsorption was governed by chemically homogeneous interactions at polar functional groups, while at near-saturation RH, the mechanism shifted toward multilayer adsorption and capillary condensation. Temperature-dependent measurements at fixed RH further revealed an unusual diffusion–reaction–diffusion transition across the studied temperature range. Across three adsorption–regeneration cycles, adsorption capacity increased progressively while the dominant kinetic model at each condition remained unchanged, indicating that regeneration preserves the fundamental water–material interaction mechanism while increasing the number of accessible active sites. These findings establish Alg-Ca@PANI–PSS as a structurally robust, reusable, and mechanistically well-characterized composite for humidity-responsive and gas-sensing applications.

item.title: Cryogenically Deposited Plasmonic Au Nanoparticle Films for Photothermal Treatment of Lung Cancer Cells
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, Au nanoparticle-coated glass substrates were fabricated by a cryogenic nonequilibrium deposition method at substrate temperatures of 300 and 230 K for plasmonic photothermal therapy applications. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy analysis revealed that the Au films deposited at 300 and 230 K consisted of nanoparticle assemblies with size distributions of approximately 7–17 nm and 8–10 nm, respectively. The significantly narrower particle size distribution observed at 230 K could be attributed to the emergence of a morphology consistent with the proposed soliton-mediated nonequilibrium growth mechanism characteristic of cryogenic deposition conditions. Atomic force microscopy measurements demonstrated that the average surface roughness decreased from 5.27 nm for the 300 K sample to 1.55 nm for the 230 K sample, confirming the formation of a more homogeneous nanoparticle architecture under cryogenic growth conditions. Optical characterization showed that both Au nanoparticle films exhibited surface plasmon resonance near 600 nm. However, the cryogenically fabricated film produced at 230 K displayed a substantially stronger plasmonic response, which was attributed to its enhanced structural uniformity and improved interparticle plasmonic coupling. To evaluate their photothermal performance, human lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells and normal bronchial epithelial BEAS-2B cells were cultured on bare-glass and Au nanoparticle-coated substrates and subsequently exposed to ∼600 nm irradiation using a 450 mW light source. Morphological and fluorescence-based analyses revealed pronounced photothermal-induced cytotoxicity in A549 cells cultured on Au-coated surfaces, including reduced cell density, disruption of cell–cell interactions, membrane damage, and loss of cellular organization. In contrast, BEAS-2B cells largely preserved their morphology, adhesion behavior, and membrane integrity under identical treatment conditions. The strongest cytotoxic response was observed for the Au nanoparticle films fabricated at 230 K. These findings suggest that cryogenic nonequilibrium deposition can improve nanoparticle uniformity and plasmonic performance, with the 230 K Au nanoparticle films producing the most pronounced photothermal response under the investigated conditions. In the preliminary biological evaluation, A549 cells exhibited a greater photothermal response than BEAS-2B cells under identical experimental conditions. These proof-of-concept findings highlight the potential of cryogenically fabricated plasmonic nanostructures for further investigation in photothermal biomedical applications.

item.title: Acoustical Materials from Conventional to Cutting-Edge Innovations─An Overview
item.description:
Abstract
With rapid urbanization and industrial expansion, noise pollution has escalated into a pervasive environmental and public health crisis. Thus, an imperative need arises for both advanced sound mitigation strategies and, especially, a fundamental shift toward sustainability to meet pressing worldwide environmental policies. The overview critically examines, unlike the already published reviews, the broad spectrum of AMs─from established conventional options to cutting-edge innovations─while consistently evaluating them through the lenses of working mechanisms, acoustic performance, and holistic sustainability (including manufacturing and life-cycle considerations). For applications where blocking airborne sound is the primary objective, natural materials with higher density and mass, such as denser types of wood or composites incorporating mass-enhancing components, should be prioritized because the acoustical properties of natural materials as soundproofing materials are influenced by a complex interplay of factors (density, mass, porosity, air permeability, thickness, internal structure, resonant frequencies, surface area, and texture). This paper systematically explores the fundamental principles of sound interaction with materials, classifying traditional, natural, hybrid, and emerging smart materials and metamaterials. The following discussion explores key performance metrics, practical applications, and the inherent challenges and future directions in the field, striving to offer a holistic perspective on the ongoing quest for effective, durable, and truly sustainable acoustic solutions. Therefore, this overview is intended to be an exhaustive, comprehensive, and valuable tool for engineers and researchers in the field of acoustic materials, with real help for saving cost and time throughout the design process. Such an overview covering all acoustic material types with elements of sustainability and future perspectives has never been reported before.

item.title: 3D Photoprintable Bismuth Methacrylate Resins: From Formulation to Printed Polymers
item.description:
Abstract
Vat photopolymerization enables the fabrication of complex geometries with high resolution, but incorporating high-density metal compounds into photocurable resins remains challenging due to sedimentation, limited dispersion, and reduced dimensional accuracy. In this work, we report 3D photoprintable resins incorporating bismuth(III) methacrylate [Bi(MA)3], as an alternative strategy for incorporating a high-Z element into photopolymer networks, enabling a largely homogeneous distribution at the bulk scale while mitigating dispersion and processing limitations associated with particulate fillers. Resin formulations included N,N-dimethylacrylamide (DMAA) as a solvent and monomer, either urethane dimethacrylate (UDMA) or poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA), a photoinitiator, and photoabsorbers. Cure depth experiments and Jacob’s working curves guided the optimization of exposure parameters and component ratios, yielding resins with reliable curing behavior at a layer thickness of 100 μm. The influence of Bi content (0–25 wt %) as Bi(MA)3 or its polymerized form was systematically assessed. Increasing the Bi(MA)3 content reduced overpolymerization in both UDMA and PEGDA systems, improving z-axis fidelity in printed structures. Mechanical testing revealed an optimal Bi loading of 10 wt % for UDMA and 20 wt % for PEGDA at which stiffness, tensile strength, and toughness were maximized. At higher Bi contents, embrittlement caused reduced toughness and lower strain at break. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy revealed a largely homogeneous bismuth distribution within the printed networks at the bulk scale, while higher Bi contents led to the formation of localized Bi-rich regions at interlayer interfaces aligned with the printing direction. These microstructural features correlate with the observed changes in mechanical behavior at elevated Bi loadings. At moderate Bi loadings, thermogravimetric analysis revealed lower decomposition temperatures, with partial recovery at higher Bi contents, while residual mass increased with Bi content, consistent with the initial Bi loading. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed glass transition temperatures of approximately 125 °C for both Bi-free and 5 wt % Bi UDMA materials, but no such transitions were observed at higher Bi contents. While polymer films without Bi and 100 μm-thick films with 10 and 20 wt % Bi content exhibited high transparency, increasing film thickness (200–500 μm) and Bi(MA)3 content led to increased opacity. Collectively, these results demonstrate that Bi(MA)3 enables the incorporation of high bismuth loadings into photocurable resins, resulting in a largely homogeneous distribution at the bulk scale. This yields materials with tunable mechanical and thermal properties while preserving printability, enhancing z-axis fidelity, and mitigating the sedimentation and dispersion issues typical of particulate fillers.

item.title: Comparative Transcriptomic and Lipidomic Analysis of Amphotericin B-Susceptible and Resistant Clinical Isolates of Malassezia spp
item.description:
Abstract
Malassezia spp. are lipid-dependent skin commensal yeasts associated with superficial infections and fungemia. Amphotericin B remains a key treatment for systemic infections despite its toxicity and decreased susceptibility. This study characterized amphotericin B susceptibility profiles and identified transcriptomic and lipidomic signatures of polyene resistance in clinical Malassezia isolates. Clinical isolates of M. sympodialis and M. furfur, and reference strains (CBS 7222 and CBS 1878), were evaluated using the modified M27-A3 CLSI protocol for MICs and subinhibitory concentrations. One isolate per species was susceptible (MIC 0.5–2.0 μg/mL), while another was resistant (MIC ≥ 16 μg/mL). Transcriptomes generated by Oxford Nanopore sequencing were analyzed using DESeq2 (|log2FC|>2, p < 0.05). Comparisons between susceptible and resistant isolates revealed few Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) that were not enriched for ergosterol biosynthesis. Interaction hubs indicated roles in nucleotide homeostasis, translation, chromatin regulation, and stress pathways. Lipidomic analysis by HPLC-QTOF-MS detected approximately 200 lipid species, including 55 Differential Lipid Molecules (DLMs) for M. sympodialis and 63 for M. furfur. Although global class abundances remained unchanged, resistant clinical isolates showed differences in the relative abundance of selected lipid species, with increased levels of long-chain fatty acids, diacylglycerols, and ceramides. Resistant M. sympodialis showed higher cholesterol levels. Integrated analysis separated susceptible and resistant groups, with DEGs–DLMs correlations highlighting networks in membrane organization, stress tolerance, and metabolism. These findings suggest that amphotericin B resistance may be associated with metabolic alterations and changes in membrane lipid composition, supporting the use of multiomics markers for detection and therapeutic strategies.

item.title: Effect of Ga Doping on Microwave-Assisted Synthesized TiO 2 Nanoparticles and their Photovoltaic Performance as DSSC Photoanodes
item.description:
Abstract
Undoped and Ga-doped (1–16% nominal) anatase TiO2 nanoparticles were synthesized using a rapid microwave-assisted method and employed as photoanodes in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) sensitized with Z907 dye. Structural, morphological, optical, and textural characterizations (XRD, Raman, SEM, DRS, BET, UV–vis, and FTIR) revealed systematic Ga-induced modifications of the anatase TiO2 structure and progressive reduction in crystallite and particle sizes, together with a significant increase in specific surface area. Moderate nominal Ga content enhanced dye adsorption and visible-light harvesting without substantially modifying the TiO2 bandgap. Photovoltaic performance, evaluated by current density–voltage (J-V) and open-circuit voltage decay (OCVD) measurements, showed that the photoanode fabricated with 4% nominal Ga content performed best, achieving an approximately 60% enhancement in power conversion efficiency compared with undoped TiO2 devices. The improved photovoltaic response is attributed to enhanced light harvesting, improved charge injection, and reduced recombination losses, driven by favorable modification of the trap-state distribution and interfacial charge-transfer processes. In contrast, higher nominal Ga contents increased the distribution of deep trap states and inefficient semiconductor-dye coupling, reducing device performance. Stability tests conducted over 30 days confirmed that TiO2-based photoanodes with a nominal 4% Ga content exhibited the best long-term photovoltaic stability. The findings demonstrate that controlled Ga doping is an effective strategy for tailoring the physicochemical and electronic properties of TiO2 photoanodes and improving DSSC performance.

item.title: Cardiolipin-Based Electrochemical Biosensor for Non-treponemal Antibody Detection Using Screen-Printed Electrodes: A Proof-of-Concept Study
item.description:
Abstract
Syphilis remains a major public health concern. Although non-treponemal tests are widely used for screening and treatment monitoring, their interpretation relies on visual assessment of flocculation. Here, an amperometric biosensor using isolated cardiolipin (0.03–0.12%) as the sole biorecognition element was developed on carbon/graphene screen-printed electrodes. The 0.06% concentration was selected for subsequent experiments, and the biosensor discriminated positive and negative control materials across two electrode batches. Progressive positive-control dilution produced a systematic electrochemical response (R2 = 0.921). Electrode functionalization significantly affected the response (p < 0.001), supporting the contribution of immobilized cardiolipin. Discrimination was maintained under physiological and pathological glucose conditions (adjusted p < 0.001). These findings provide a preliminary proof-of-concept for cardiolipin-based electrochemical assessment of non-treponemal antibody reactivity. Further studies using clinical samples are required to establish analytical and clinical performance and investigate semiquantitative evaluation by correlating electrochemical responses with defined serological titers.

item.title: Fabrication and Characterization of 3D-Printed Polylactide Composite Scaffolds with Modified Graphene
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, we introduce novel multifunctional biomaterial inks for extrusion-based 3D bioprinting to create scaffolds for potential tissue engineering. This study focuses on developing composite materials by incorporating alkyl ketene dimer (AKD)-modified graphene nanoplatelets (GP) into polylactide (PLA) using a solvent casting technique. GP was synthesized via electrolytic exfoliation in an aqueous poly(sodium 4-styrenesulfonate) solution and subsequently modified with AKD by ball milling to enhance dispersion and PLA compatibility. Physical and chemical characterization confirmed the successful synthesis and structural properties of the AKD-modified GP. PLA-GPD20 films containing 20 wt % AKD-modified GP exhibited significantly improved elongation at break and maintained tensile strength comparable to neat PLA. All biomaterial composite films exhibited high stiffness, as evidenced by glass transition temperatures above room temperature, and electrical conductivity in the semiconductor range. The results highlight the significant positive impact of AKD on the physical and electrical properties, as well as the printability, of the composites. The printability performance potential was evaluated using 10 wt % PLA-GPD20 biomaterial inks to generate scaffolds with different patterns. The mechanical testing of the printed scaffolds revealed that the tensile strength and modulus increased with the incorporation of GPD20. The printing orientation is an effective parameter for tuning the balance between stiffness and ductility; scaffolds printed at 90° exhibited higher Young’s modulus but lower elongation at yield and tensile strength than those printed at 45°. Furthermore, incorporating AKD into GP/PLA composites improved hydrophobicity. The results suggest that AKD-modified graphene composites hold substantial promise for the development of advanced multifunctional materials for tissue engineering applications.

item.title: Tuning Molecular Transformations and Accumulation of Reactive Species in Plasma-Treated Liquids via Organic Biomolecules
item.description:
Abstract
Plasma processing of liquids is a sustainable platform for green chemistry and biomedical applications, enabling the synthesis of inorganic and organic molecules without harmful reagents and with compatibility with renewable electricity. PTWS constitute reservoirs of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, and their composition is governed not only by the experimental conditions of the plasma employed for their generation, but also, and predominantly, by the chemical composition of the precursor liquid. In this study, we demonstrate that organic solutes actively modulate RONS chemistry. Phenolic compounds such as l-tyrosine and resorcinol enhance H2O2 production while differently affecting nitrogen species, leading to either scavenging or overproduction of NO2–. Mass spectrometry reveals a strong correlation between molecular structure, plasma-induced modifications, and resulting RONS dynamics. These findings redefine PTWS as dynamic, reactive environments rather than passive reservoirs by also explaining the prolonged activity of such liquids. Beyond plasma medicine, they provide a framework for optimizing RONS-based therapies and contribute to the broader understanding of nonequilibrium chemistry in complex liquids. The results also open opportunities in water treatment and sustainable chemical transformations, positioning PTWS as versatile tools for controlling redox processes in complex aqueous systems.

item.title: Ecotoxicological Effects of a Commercial Fenthion-Based Formulation on the Survival, Hatching, and Growth of Artemia salina L.: Implications for Risk Assessment in Marine and Estuarine Environments
item.description:
Abstract
This present study evaluated the effects of a commercial formulation based on fenthion on survival, hatching, and growth of Artemia salina, and characterized the environmental risk of this insecticide to marine and estuarine ecosystems. The fenthion-based commercial formulation was tested at concentrations ranging from 0.001 up to 731 mg/L using different bioassays: a standard 48-h acute test, a 14-day long-term test, and also two 72-h assays (one for cyst hatching, another for growth inhibition). Obtained EC50 values were fully integrated with available literature data to construct a species sensitivity distribution (SSD) curve, which then determined the hazardous concentration for 5% of species (HC5), the predicted no-effect concentration (PNEC), and the risk quotient (RQ). In the acute assay, the formulation showed low toxicity, with EC50 of 212.36 mg/L at 24 h and 16.64 mg/L at 48 h. In contrast, high toxicity was observed in long-term tests, with EC50 of 0.0752 mg/L after 8 days and 0.0052 mg/L after 14 days of exposure. Minor effects were observed on hatching rate (EC50 = 101.75 mg/L), whereas more pronounced effects were seen on hatching speed (EC50 = 19.88 mg/L) and nauplii growth (EC10 = 0.076 mg/L). The HC5 from the SSD was 0.000104 mg/L, while PNEC was 0.000020 mg/L. The average RQ was 1.86, indicating high risk. Overall, these results demonstrate the ecotoxicological potential of a fenthion-based commercial formulation for relevant organisms in marine and estuarine ecosystems, reinforcing the importance of regulatory measures and environmental monitoring in areas subject to contamination by this insecticide.

item.title: Single-Excitation, Orthogonally Encoded Quantum Dot Probes for Dual-Mode Multiplexed Biosensing
item.description:
Abstract
Simultaneous quantitative detection of multiple rheumatoid arthritis (RA) biomarkers is often constrained by the need for separate analytical platforms and complex instrumentation. Here, we describe a dual-mode multiplex immunoassay that integrates a lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) with a magnetic bead immunoassay (MBIA) using spectrally resolved SiO2-encapsulated quantum dot (SiO2@QDs) probes. By combining SiO2@CdSe and carbon dot-based SiO2 nanoparticles, three spectrally distinct fluorescence signals (blue, green, and red) were generated under single-wavelength excitation (365 nm), enabling concurrent detection of anticyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies (anti-CCP), rheumatoid factor IgM (RF-IgM), and C-reactive protein (CRP). The LFIA module enables multiplex quantification within 10 min with minimal instrumentation, whereas the MBIA module extends analytical sensitivity and dynamic range through homogeneous immunoreactions and magnetic separation. The limits of detection of the MBIA sensor were 0.142 U/mL for anti-CCP, 0.057 IU/mL for RF-IgM, and 0.075 mg/L for CRP, with linear responses (R2 > 0.98), coefficients of variation below 8%, and minimal cross-reactivity. Analysis of clinical RA samples showed good agreement with commercial reference assays, as assessed by Passing–Bablok regression and Bland–Altman analysis. By integrating rapid screening and laboratory-grade quantification within a single fluorescence-encoded nanoprobe system, this dual-mode platform illustrates a modular strategy for multiplex autoimmune biomarker analysis, in which assay format and signal encoding are decoupled within a unified optical framework.

item.title: Processing-Tuned Laser-Induced Graphene Transducers for Polyaniline pH Sensors
item.description:
Abstract
Flexible pH sensors are important for wearable, biomedical, environmental, and process-monitoring applications, but achieving simple, scalable fabrication while maintaining high sensing performance remains challenging. Laser-induced graphene (LIG) has emerged as a promising transducer material because it enables direct laser patterning of porous, conductive graphitized carbon electrodes on flexible substrates. Although laser-processing conditions are known to affect LIG morphology, graphitization, and electrical properties, their influence on pH-sensitive layer formation and pH-sensing performance has not been systematically investigated. In this study, polyaniline (PANi)-modified LIG pH sensors were fabricated using four laser-processing combinations of laser power and scan speed. The resulting LIG and PANi/LIG electrodes were characterized using sheet-resistance measurements, optical microscopy, SEM, Raman spectroscopy, and XPS. PANi was electropolymerized on the LIG working electrodes under identical cyclic voltammetry conditions, and the assembled sensors were evaluated in pH 4–9 buffer solutions. The results showed that laser processing produced distinct LIG morphologies, porosities, sheet resistance, and PANi coverage, leading to different sensing performances. Among the samples, PANi/LIG-9.2–350, fabricated at 9.2 W and 350 mm/s, exhibited the best overall performance, with a near-Nernstian sensitivity of −60.04 mV/pH, a 12 h drift rate of 1.67 mV/h, hysteresis of 2.06 mV, and rapid response time of 13.2 s. These findings emphasize the significance of laser-processing-dependent LIG microstructure and electrical properties in governing PANi deposition behavior and resulting potentiometric pH-sensing performance.

item.title: Experimental and DFT Investigation of Crystal Violet Biosorption by Taraxacum officinale Leaf Biomass
item.description:
Abstract
Leaf powder obtained from wild Taraxacum officinale was directly used as a biosorbent for the removal of Crystal Violet (CV), a widely used cationic dye, because the leaves are rich in fibers and minerals and have not previously been employed in their untreated form for biosorption. Standard instrumental analyses were employed for the identification of surface functional groups (FT-IR), imaging of surface morphology (FE-SEM), and elemental characterization (EDX). Adsorption was favored under alkaline conditions, reaching a maximum removal efficiency of 46.53% at pH 12, corresponding to an experimental adsorption capacity of 149.1 mg g–1, while adsorbent dosages between 100 and 200 mg were effective for dye removal. The untreated biomass surface exhibited adsorption-favoring grooves and stomata. Taraxacum officinale biomass exhibited a lignocellulosic structure, with carbon and oxygen contents of 54.26 and 42.46 at%, respectively. Adsorption equilibrium was best described by the nonlinear Langmuir model (R2 = 0.948), supporting monolayer adsorption onto a relatively homogeneous surface. The D–R model further supported a physicochemical adsorption mechanism. Frontier molecular orbital (FMO) and natural bond orbital (NBO) analyses were performed at the B3LYP/6-311++G** level in both gas and aqueous media to elucidate the electronic interactions between CV and the lignocellulosic surface.

item.title: Porosity Engineering of Eggshell-Derived Nanostructured Hydroxyapatite for Ethanol Upgrading: Structural, Textural and Surface Characterization
item.description:
Abstract
Hydroxyapatite (HAp) has attracted considerable attention as a catalyst owing to its tunable acid–base properties; however, the influence of porogen-assisted synthesis on its textural characteristics and catalytic behavior remains insufficiently understood. In this work, nanostructured HAp was synthesized via a sol–gel route using calcium precursors derived from chicken eggshell waste, combining waste valorization with sustainable catalyst design. The results demonstrate a relationship between porogen-assisted modification of eggshell-derived hydroxyapatite, the resulting textural and acid–base properties, and the relative n-butanol yield obtained during relative n-butanol yield under the investigated conditions. The incorporation of pore-forming agents modified the textural properties of HAp, increasing the specific surface area from approximately 28 to 155 m2 g–1 and enhancing the pore volume. Nitrogen adsorption–desorption analyses revealed mesoporous structures with pore sizes ranging from 5 to 35 nm, while the glucose-templated sample exhibited a bimodal pore-size distribution indicative of porosity. The increase in surface area and pore accessibility improved the availability of acid–base active sites, as confirmed by NH3-TPD and CO2-TPD measurements. A structure–activity relationship was observed, with the most porous catalysts achieving relative n-butanol yields above 87%, based on normalized GC peak areas at 180 °C. Product distribution analysis based on gas chromatographic peak areas revealed enhanced relative n-butanol yields and improved selectivity toward n-butanol formation for catalysts with higher surface areas and mesoporosity. These findings demonstrate that waste-derived eggshells can be effectively converted into porous hydroxyapatite catalysts with tunable textural and acid–base properties, offering a sustainable approach for ethanol upgrading toward n-butanol.

item.title: CB-Smart: A Cloud-Based Machine Learning Platform for Screening Cannabinoid Receptor Ligands
item.description:
Abstract
Cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2 are class A G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) implicated in pain modulation, neuroinflammation, immune regulation, and metabolic processes, making them important therapeutic targets. Conventional structure-based virtual screening for cannabinoid ligands remains computationally intensive and limited in throughput. To overcome this challenge, this work presents CB-Smart, a cloud-enabled machine learning (ML) platform to predict binding of ligands and their relative binding affinity to CB1 and CB2. Using curated experimentally validated ligands and GPCR decoy datasets, we trained five supervised ML algorithms, XGBoost, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). Three featurization strategies, ECFP molecular fingerprints, RDKit 210 molecular descriptors, and Lipinski descriptors, were systematically evaluated. Models built on ECFP fingerprint features, particularly XGBoost, SVM, and MLP, demonstrated the highest performance on both reserved test datasets and an external dataset. A hard-voting ensemble integrating the top three classifiers further enhanced predictive performance. Further, SHAP-based interpretability analysis highlighted key structural and physicochemical drivers of cannabinoid receptor binding, offering insights into ligand-receptor interactions and structure-activity relationships. Finally, we integrated classification and regression models into an interactive, user-friendly cloud platform, enabling broad accessibility for virtual screening, medicinal chemistry optimization and early-stage drug discovery efforts targeting cannabinoid receptors.

item.title: A Deep Learning Approach for Thickness Determination of AZO Thin Films
item.description:
Abstract
We developed a database and a machine learning model to predict the thickness of aluminum-doped zinc oxide (AZO) thin films from their optical transmittance spectra. We measured the spectra of 145 thin films with thicknesses between 100 and 1500 nm and fitted each with a 12-parameter function, one parameter being the film thickness. We divided the thickness range into five regions and modeled the distribution of each fitting parameter in each region as a sum of Gaussian functions. Random sampling from these distributions produced parameter sets used to construct synthetic transmittance spectra (X), each paired with its film thickness (Y) to form one database sample (X, Y). We generated 240,000 samples per region, yielding a database of 1.2 million samples for supervised training with thickness as the target. The initial machine learning model, a fully connected neural network, showed poor predictive accuracy. We therefore improved the architecture by incorporating an autoencoder with skip connections to extract the most informative features from the transmittance spectra. This change substantially improved performance, yielding mean absolute errors of 15.8(3) nm on the training set and 15.7(3) nm on the validation set. When applied to the transmittance spectra of the experimental AZO films, the trained model predicted thicknesses with a mean absolute percentage error of 6.91%. Because the model was trained using data derived from AZO measurements, it applies only to AZO thin films. The methodology, however, is general and can be applied to thin films of any composition.

item.title: Effects of Carbon Functionalization on Pd/C Electrocatalysts for Alcohol Oxidation and Alkaline Direct Alcohol Fuel Cells
item.description:
Abstract
This study examines how KOH and HNO3 pretreatment of Vulcan XC-72 changes the physicochemical and electrochemical behavior of Pd/C catalysts for CO, ethanol, and glycerol oxidation in alkaline media. Pd nanoparticles were deposited by borohydride reduction. The treatments increased the BET surface area but decreased the measured Pd content, while altering oxygen functionalities, the Pd0/Pd2+ surface distribution, and the particle-size distribution. Electrochemical results showed that these structural and surface changes were associated with differences in the electrochemical response of the catalysts rather than being governed solely by electrochemically accessible surface area. Pd supported on KOH-treated carbon (Pd/CKOH) showed the lowest electrochemically active surface area but the highest ECSA-normalized peak current densities for ethanol and glycerol oxidation, whereas Pd/C HNO3 showed the lowest ethanol oxidation onset potential. Relative to Pd/C, the CO oxidation onset shifted negatively by 70 mV for Pd/CKOH and 40 mV for Pd/C HNO3, accompanied by treatment-dependent differences in the CO-stripping profiles. The alcohol oxidation onset potentials and peak current-density rankings depended on the alcohol and did not follow a single catalyst descriptor. Single-cell alkaline direct alcohol fuel cell tests further showed that normalization by the actual Pd loading affected the catalyst comparison. On a Pd-mass basis, Pd/CKOH exhibited the highest peak current and power densities for both ethanol and glycerol at all tested temperatures. Overall, the results indicate that support pretreatment is associated with concurrent changes in support surface chemistry, Pd surface chemical state, crystallographic texture, and electrochemical response, which together accompany the observed differences in electrocatalytic performance. These findings highlight the importance of considering multiple physicochemical and electrochemical descriptors, as well as catalyst loading and operating conditions, when evaluating the effects of carbon-support functionalization on Pd-based electrocatalysts.

item.title: Hydrodynamic Studies of Cocrystal under Nonsink Dissolution on Orbital Shaker
item.description:
Abstract
The dissolution behavior of pharmaceutical cocrystals, particularly under nonsink conditions, is influenced by operational parameters such as Erlenmeyer flask size and rotation speed. This study investigates the hydrodynamic impacts of these variables on the dissolution of lamotrigine-nicotinamide (LAM-NIC) cocrystals using experimental and computational approaches. Dissolution experiments were conducted in orbital shakers with 125 and 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks at 50, 100, and 150 rpm. The results showed that the Erlenmeyer flask size and rotation speed significantly affect the dissolution profile, with the 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask at 100 rpm providing the most favorable conditions among those investigated for revealing the supersaturated state. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations modeled the fluid dynamics within the flasks, providing insights into the velocity and strain rate profiles under different conditions. A higher tangential velocity and strain rate at 100 rpm correlated with enhanced cocrystal dissolution in the 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask, whereas the smaller flask showed a limited variation across rotation speeds. These findings emphasize the importance of hydrodynamic conditions in dissolution studies and support the development of standardized methodologies for assessing cocrystal performance under nonsink conditions. This research contributes to optimizing the design of supersaturating drug delivery systems and understanding the interplay between the hydrodynamics and cocrystal behavior.

item.title: Coupling Characteristics and Sensitivity Differences of Coal Porosity and Permeability with Stress in Different Wellfields of Fukang Mining Area
item.description:
Abstract
Quantifying how coal porosity and permeability vary with effective stress is essential for forecasting coalbed methane (CBM) deliverability, yet the coupled stress response of low-rank coals and its variation among wellfields remain poorly constrained. Nine cores from three wellfields of the Fukang mining area─Kuangou (KG), Wudong (WD), and Donggou (DG)─were tested under stepwise hydrostatic loading of 2.07–15.86 MPa while porosity and permeability were measured simultaneously. Both properties decrease exponentially with stress, but permeability declines far more strongly: at maximum loading, the porosity damage ratio ranges from 15.9% to 69.55%, whereas the permeability damage ratio reaches 82.2–96.7%, and permeability sensitivity across wellfields follows DG ≈ WD > KG. A porosity–permeability ratio (e = φ/k) and a relative sensitivity parameter (R) were introduced to quantify the storage–seepage mismatch, with e rising continuously along the loading path. Fracture density, aperture, pore-throat connectivity, and mineral infilling jointly govern the heterogeneous response. The results provide quantitative criteria for staged depressurization and fracturing design in low-rank CBM development.

item.title: Natural Product-Derived Hydrogels for Myocardial Infarction Repair: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Translational Perspectives
item.description:
Abstract
Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of death worldwide, yet current therapeutic interventions offer limited capacity for functional cardiac regeneration. In recent years, hydrogels derived from natural products have emerged as compelling therapeutic platforms, attributed to their favorable biocompatibility, tunable biodegradability, and intrinsic biological activities. This review systematically summarizes natural product-derived hydrogels for MI repair, with particular emphasis on representative polysaccharide-based systems, including chitosan, alginate, and hyaluronic acid. It also discusses small-molecule self-assembled hydrogels, such as glycyrrhizic acid, puerarin, and rhein, as well as hydrogel-based extracellular vesicle delivery systems, as complementary therapeutic strategies. We further highlight the multifaceted mechanisms through which these materials ameliorate the pathological cardiac microenvironment, including structural reinforcement, restoration of electrical conduction, modulation of the immune response, promotion of neovascularization, and scavenging of reactive oxygen species. Critical challenges impeding clinical translation, such as long-term biocompatibility, targeted delivery efficiency, and scalable manufacturing, are thoroughly examined, alongside emerging directions including stimuli-responsive systems and three-dimensional bioprinting technologies. Although natural product-derived hydrogels hold considerable promise for cardiac repair, overcoming existing technical hurdles through continued interdisciplinary research remains imperative for their successful transition from bench to bedside.

item.title: Targeting Caveolin-1 Alleviated Diabetic Retinopathy Injury through Protecting Müller Cells from Ferroptosis via the xCT/GPX4 Signaling Pathway
item.description:
Abstract
Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a global blinding eye disease, and its early pathological features are closely associated with retinal Müller cell dysfunction. Caveolin-1 (Cav-1) is a protein widely expressed in mammalian tissues and participates in regulating Müller cell function; however, its role in DR remains unclear. This study provides evidence that Cav-1 alleviates DR pathology and elucidates the underlying mechanisms. Müller cells were treated with high glucose, and diabetes was induced in Sprague–Dawley rats by streptozotocin injection. Cav-1 expression levels were modulated using the Caveolin-1 scaffolding domain peptide CSD, as well as Cav-1 knockdown or overexpression. The results showed that under high glucose stress, inhibition of Cav-1 expression significantly reduced intracellular ACSL4 protein levels, ROS levels, MDA and Fe2+ concentrations, while increasing GSH content and the protein expression of SLC7A11 and GPX4. Notably, treatment with the GPX4 inhibitor RSL3 abolished this protective effect, confirming the involvement of the xCT/GPX4 pathway in Cav-1-mediated protection. In vivo, CSD treatment exerted protective effects as early as week 8. Electron microscopy revealed that, compared with diabetic rats, CSD treatment ameliorated mitochondrial edema and restored mitochondrial cristae structure. Furthermore, immunofluorescence staining showed spatial consistency between Cav-1 protein expression and Müller cell localization. These findings indicate that targeting Cav-1 alleviates oxidative stress, reduces ferroptosis, and ameliorates early-stage DR injury by activating the xCT/GPX4 signaling pathway, suggesting that Cav-1 targeting may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for DR.

item.title: Experimental Study on the Inhibition of Hydrogen/Methane/Air Explosion by Potassium Oxalate Water Mist
item.description:
Abstract
The suppression characteristics of hydrogen/methane/air explosion by water mist with potassium oxalate (K2C2O4·H2O) additive were experimentally investigated in this work. The effects of pure water mist and K2C2O4·H2O-modified water mist on flame morphology, average flame propagation speed, maximum flame acceleration, explosion pressure, and maximum pressure rise rate were systematically analyzed. Results indicated that the inhibition efficiency of pure water mist is limited and reaches saturation with increasing concentration, while the addition of K2C2O4·H2O significantly enhances the explosion suppression performance. With the increase of K2C2O4·H2O mass fraction, the average flame propagation speed and maximum flame acceleration are gradually reduced, the peak explosion pressure and maximum pressure rise rate are observably decreased, and the time to reach peak pressure is obviously delayed. When the mass fraction of K2C2O4·H2O is above 6%, the pressure evolution curve is transformed from a three-stage mode to a four-stage mode. Based on TG-DSC experimental analysis, the thermal decomposition process of K2C2O4·H2O is determined as dehydration and decomposition to produce K2CO3 and CO. The physical–chemical synergistic explosion suppression mechanism is revealed, in which physical effects including endothermic cooling, inert dilution, and flame destruction provide favorable conditions for chemical inhibition, and chemical chain termination reduces heat release and strengthens physical suppression. The findings can provide theoretical support for the safety protection of hydrogen/methane/air systems.

item.title: Chirality as a Structural Degree of Freedom in Halide Perovskites
item.description:
Abstract
Chirality in halide perovskites has traditionally been associated with the incorporation of intrinsically chiral molecular components. Here, we develop a broader perspective in which chirality can emerge from the collective structural organization of an otherwise achiral inorganic lattice. We distinguish the structural origins of chirality, including molecular or ligand-mediated interactions, cooperative lattice distortions, surfaces and interfaces, and dynamic structural fluctuations, from the thermodynamic and structural parameters that control these states, including strain, dimensionality, confinement, temperature, pressure, and composition. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing structural distortion and inversion symmetry breaking from genuine chirality, which requires the absence of all improper symmetry operations and sufficient spatial correlation of the handed structural state. Two halide perovskite systems, Cs2PbI2Cl2 nanoplatelets and CsPbBr3 nanorods, illustrate complementary examples in which structural perturbations are associated with pronounced chiroptical responses. We further outline experimental criteria for establishing structural chirality and discuss opportunities for selecting, switching, and coupling handed structural states to optical, electronic, spin, and magnetic functionalities.

item.title: Reignition Behavior Evolution and Microscopic Kinetic Mechanism of Lignite at Various Preoxidation Temperatures
item.description:
Abstract
In order to reveal the evolution characteristics and microdynamic mechanism of the reignition behavior of Shajihai coal at different preoxidation temperatures, this paper systematically studied the differences in the spontaneous-combustion characteristics of Shajihai coal at different preoxidation temperatures (40, 70, 100, 130, 160 °C) by means of temperature-programmed experiments, simultaneous thermal analysis (TG-DSC), in situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and other experimental methods. The results show that the preoxidation temperature has a nonlinear regulation effect on the spontaneous-combustion tendency of Shajihai coal. In the high temperature stage (>160 °C), the release of CO and CO2 increased by 16% and 9.7%, respectively, compared with the raw coal, indicating that its oxidation activity was the strongest. However, the oxidation activity of preoxidized coal at 130–160 °C was inhibited due to the consumption of active groups caused by high-temperature pyrolysis, and the most prominent passivation effect occurs at 160 °C. FTIR analysis showed that the oxygen-containing functional groups (−OH, C═O) of the preoxidized 100 °C coal sample were slightly reduced by 3%–9.6% compared with the raw coal, and the aliphatic hydrocarbon content was increased by 33%–42% compared with the raw coal. The conversion rate of functional groups in the high temperature stage (230–300 °C) was accelerated, which further aggravated the chain reaction. This study realizes the coupling interpretation of macroscopic reignition performance and microscopic molecular evolution by combining programmed-temperature gas test, TG-DSC, and in situ FTIR measurements.

item.title: Ultrasonic-Assisted Stir Casting of SiO 2 -Reinforced AA7075: Microstructure, Strengthening, and Wear
item.description:
Abstract
The present work examines the effect of SiO2 nanoparticle addition on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and dry-sliding wear behavior of AA7075-based metal matrix nanocomposites. Four reinforcement levels, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 wt %, were investigated. AA7075 was reinforced with SiO2 using an ultrasonic-assisted stir-casting process. The process produced relatively uniform SiO2 distributions up to 1.5 wt % and a refined aluminum matrix, whereas localized particle-rich regions became evident at 2.0 wt %. The tensile strength increased from 190 ± 15 MPa for the unreinforced alloy to 255 ± 22, 310 ± 10, 360 ± 22, and 385 ± 12 MPa for composites containing 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 wt % SiO2, respectively, corresponding to strength improvements of approximately 34.2%, 63.2%, 89.5%, and 102.6%. Microhardness also increased from 86 ± 3 VHV for AA7075 to 164 ± 12 VHV for the composite containing 2.0 wt % SiO2. The improvements in strength and hardness are consistent with matrix refinement, interfacial load transfer, restriction of dislocation motion, and thermal-expansion-mismatch-induced dislocation strengthening. Dry-sliding wear experiments were conducted in accordance with ASTM G99 at a sliding velocity of 3.14 m s–1, a total sliding distance of 6 km, and applied loads of 10–50 N. The reinforced materials generally showed lower specific wear rates than the unreinforced alloy. At 50 N, the specific wear rate decreased from approximately 6900 to 4500 μm3 N–1 mm–1 with the addition of 2.0 wt % SiO2, corresponding to a decrease of approximately 34.8%. The coefficient of friction generally decreased with increasing SiO2 content, and the 2.0 wt % composite exhibited the lowest values within the investigated range. SEM and TEM examinations provided evidence of changes in particle distribution and microstructural features with increasing reinforcement content, while SEM examination of the worn surfaces revealed corresponding changes in wear morphology. Overall, the present findings show that the ultrasonic-assisted stir-casting route used in this study produced AA7075–SiO2 metal matrix nanocomposites with increased strength and hardness and generally improved dry-sliding wear behavior within the investigated composition and test range.

item.title: Halogen-Substitution of Benzotriazolium Cations Unlocks Enhanced Lewis Acidity
item.description:
Abstract
Nitrenium cations have seen a surge of interest for catalytic applications as they are inexpensive, robust, and have high tunability. Thus far, this tunability has focused on modification of the wingtip, N-bound substituents or the employment of alternative aryl scaffolds. Here, we report the systematic modification of the benzotriazolium cation by installing a variety of halogen substitution patterns to the aryl backbone. Computational investigations suggested that these modifications would increase the Lewis acidity of the nitrenium center, which was supported experimentally by the Gutmann–Beckett test. The series of novel cations were employed as Lewis acid catalysts in a model reaction, and the most Lewis acidic derivative exhibited significantly enhanced catalytic performance relative to the parent, unsubstituted benzotriazolium cation. We further examined the relative stabilities of the neutral radical forms of these derivatives through a combined experimental and computational approach.

item.title: Numerical Assessment of the Effects of Oxygen-Enriched Secondary Air on Fouling-Related Combustion Conditions in a Grate Furnace
item.description:
Abstract
Heat transfer surface fouling severely threatens the safe and efficient operation of municipal solid waste (MSW) grate incinerators and is closely linked to local oxygen-deficient combustion atmospheres. Oxygen-enriched secondary air has been investigated as an approach for modifying furnace combustion conditions; however, its influence on fouling-related combustion conditions remains insufficiently understood. This study adopts computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to investigate combustion behaviors under four secondary air oxygen mass fraction conditions: 0.21, 0.26, 0.31, and 0.36. The O2 and CO characteristics, temperature distribution, and near-wall gas phase features are compared. Simulation results demonstrate spatially nonuniform responses to secondary air oxygen enrichment. Increasing the inlet oxygen fraction reshapes the overall furnace oxygen field, yet near-wall monitoring points exhibit no monotonic increase in local oxygen content. The CO/CO2 and H2/H2O ratios stay at very low levels for all operating scenarios, and the temperature response is also spatially nonuniform. Since changing the secondary air O2/N2 composition simultaneously changes mixture density, mass flow rate, momentum flux, Reynolds number, and total oxygen supply, the obtained results reflect combined system responses rather than the independent effect of oxygen concentration. The present CFD model focuses on gas-phase combustion and excludes detailed particle transport, ash transformation, mineral phase evolution, and deposition mechanisms; hence, it only assesses relative variations of fouling-related combustion conditions and cannot directly quantify ash deposition rates or fouling suppression performance. No single optimal secondary air oxygen enrichment level is determined among the investigated cases. This work provides a numerical basis for assessing the influence of oxygen-enriched secondary air on fouling-related combustion conditions in the grate furnaces.

item.title: PDA-CeO 2 Functionalized Pickering Microcapsules with Enhanced Foliar Retention and UV Stability for Efficient Pesticide Delivery
item.description:
Abstract
Pesticide spraying applications often encounter challenges such as inadequate foliar deposition, low retention, and rapid photodegradation, which can significantly impact pesticide utilization. Microencapsulation of pesticides offers a viable solution to these issues. In this study, we encapsulated pyraclostrobin (PYR) within polydopamine-CeO2 modified polyurea microcapsules (PYR@PDA-CeO2–PU MCs) using Pickering emulsion interfacial polymerization. The PDA-modified CeO2 nanoparticles (PDA-CeO2 NPs) acted as the primary emulsifier and ultraviolet (UV) absorber, providing enhanced adhesion, controlled release, and UV protection. The PYR@PDA-CeO2–PU MCs demonstrated an encapsulation efficiency of 82.22 ± 2.00% and a loading capacity of 41.00 ± 1.50%, with a release profile consistent with the Higuchi model. The incorporation of PDA significantly improved leaf retention and adhesion, while the covalent attachment of PDA-CeO2 to the PU shell enhanced the photostability of PYR. After 72 h of UV irradiation, PYR@PDA-CeO2–PU MCs achieved a retention rate of 82.55 ± 0.80%, compared to 74.82 ± 0.44% for Seltima and 53.11 ± 0.91% for PYR TC. In vivo tests on rice and kiwifruit leaves demonstrated superior protective and curative effects, while toxicity assessments indicated reduced toxicity to zebrafish compared to PYR TC. In conclusion, the PDA-CeO2 functionalized PU MCs exhibit remarkable foliar retention and UV stability, thereby enhancing the practical application of pesticides.

item.title: Disentangling the Thermochemical and Thermodynamic Properties of Triadimefon
item.description:
Abstract
Triadimefon is a widely used systemic triazole fungicide, yet its heat capacity and enthalpy of solution, which are key thermodynamic data for reactor heat transfer design, formulation process optimization, and environmental fate modeling, remain unreported. Herein, the molar heat capacity (Cp,m) of triadimefon was measured by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) using the sapphire three-step method over the range 283.15–333.15 K. The temperature dependence of Cp,m is well described by a cubic polynomial, and Cp,m at 298.15 K is 359.23 J mol–1 K–1. The thermodynamic functions HT – H298.15 K and ST – S298.15 K were derived from the experimental heat-capacity data. These quantities, together with Cp,m, were also calculated by density functional theory. The calculated values are slightly lower than the experimental ones, with relative deviations ranging from 8.70 to 10.25%. To further understand its solution behavior, the dissolution of triadimefon in N,N-dimethylformamide was investigated at 298.15 K. The process is endothermic, with a molar dissolution enthalpy of 15.71 ± 0.13 kJ mol–1. An empirical relationship between dissolution enthalpy and molality is established, with the dissolution kinetics described by dαdt=10−2.42(1−α)0.80. The present thermochemical and kinetic results of triadimefon afford reliable bases of physical and chemical properties for formulation development, recrystallization process optimization, and environmental behavior assessment.

item.title: Extraction and Multidimensional Characterization of Pore Fractures in Gradient Thermally Treated Shale Using Micro-CT
item.description:
Abstract
Thermal stimulation is a cutting-edge technology for improving shale matrix permeability and achieving efficient shale gas development, as heating can reshape shale pore structures and enhance reservoir percolation capacity. Currently, numerous studies have revealed basic thermal-action laws and clarified the intrinsic relationship between temperature and shale reservoir structures. Nevertheless, most previous tests adopt several discrete temperature points, and quantitative descriptions of successive pore-fracture evolution in the high-temperature range under equal-interval temperature gradients are still lacking. This restricts theoretical support for optimizing field thermal-simulation parameters. To fill this gap, shale samples gradient-treated at 50–300 °C are investigated. Micro-CT scanning, ImageJ, FracLac, and Avizo are employed for two-dimensional statistics and three-dimensional reconstruction. Pore-fracture parameters, fractal dimension, and lacunarity are extracted. Complementary SEM observations at 100 and 250 °C corroborate CT-derived pore-fracture features at these two temperatures. Permeability curves covering 50–300 °C gradient series are further plotted, whose overall trend agrees well with pore-fracture structural variations captured by CT reconstruction. The results show that pore quantity and porosity decrease initially and then rise with increasing temperature. The maximum porosity appears at 300 °C, and the most complicated pore frameworks are formed at 200 °C. Fractal dimension effectively characterizes the spatial heterogeneity evolution of thermally modified shale pore networks, providing insights for shale gas thermal stimulation applications.

item.title: Numerical Simulation and Field Validation of Airflow Field and CO Dispersion Characteristics during Tunnel Construction under Dynamic Vehicle Movement
item.description:
Abstract
During tunnel construction, a substantial amount of pollutants, such as carbon monoxide, are generated. Compared with the blasting phase, the CO produced by internal combustion engines during the mucking phase exhibited continuity owing to temporal accumulation and had a wider range of influence. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate CO dispersion characteristics under different ventilation modes at various construction stages. In this study, to reveal the influence mechanism of the coupled effect of traffic-induced wind and mechanical ventilation on the airflow field and pollutant migration under dynamic vehicle movement during the tunnel mucking phase, a construction ventilation model was established based on the overset grid method. The effects of mucking truck speed, mechanical wind velocity, and truck travel direction on CO dispersion patterns under different ventilation modes were systematically analyzed. The results show that under forced ventilation conditions, a stable traffic-induced wake was generated by the dynamic movement of the vehicle in the mechanically ventilated stable zone, whereas airflow field fluctuations and multiple turbulent structures were induced in the recirculation zone near the tunnel face, where the peak airflow velocity was reduced by 47.33%. The CO concentration exhibited an annular spatial distribution pattern, characterized by higher concentrations in the central region and lower concentrations toward the periphery, and residual accumulation was formed along the vehicle travel path, with the CO dispersion range extending to 256 m after 45 s of travel. Both the peak CO concentration and the residual time of CO were effectively reduced by increasing the travel speed of the mucking truck or mechanical wind velocity. For every 2.5 km/h increment in travel speed, the peak CO concentration was reduced by 8.13% to 20.4%, and for every 5 m/s increase in wind velocity, the peak CO concentration was reduced by 0.47% to 3.74%. More favorable CO dispersion conditions were observed when the truck traveled in the downwind direction. The peak CO concentration was found to increase initially and then stabilize with prolonged ventilation time, and the CO diffusion coefficient was enhanced by increasing either the truck speed or mechanical wind velocity. This study provides a basis for optimizing ventilation parameters and controlling vehicle emissions during the tunnel mucking phase.

item.title: Identification and Characterization of a Cytosolic Malate Dehydrogenase as a Potential Drug Target in Echinococcus multilocularis
item.description:
Abstract
Alveolar echinococcosis, caused by the larval stage (metacestode) of Echinococcus multilocularis, is an emerging zoonotic disease with limited treatment options, highlighting the need for new therapeutic targets. Like other helminths, E. multilocularis relies on anaerobic metabolism via malate dismutation, a poorly characterized pathway. In this study, cytosolic malate dehydrogenase (cMDH), a key enzyme in this pathway, was investigated as a potential drug target. Bioinformatic analyses identified three cMDH homologues in E. multilocularis, all exhibiting canonical domain architecture and clustering with metazoan orthologs. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that EmuJ_000417100 (EmcMDH) is highly expressed in both in vitro-cultured metacestode vesicles and parasite lesions in mice, whereas other paralogs show minimal expression. Recombinant EmcMDH catalyzed the reversible conversion of malate and oxaloacetate, displaying typical cMDH kinetics with higher catalytic efficiency and lower Km values for oxaloacetate (16.4 ± 3.2 μM) and NADH (11.5 ± 3.9 μM) compared to malate (0.21 ± 0.10 mM) and NAD+ (0.43 ± 0.11 mM), indicating a preference for oxaloacetate reduction. RNAi-mediated knockdown of EmcMDH impaired metacestode vesicle development, demonstrating its important role in parasite growth. The natural compound gossypol potently inhibited EmcMDH (IC50 = 0.25 ± 0.04 μM) with ∼80-fold selectivity over murine cMDH. As proof-of-concept, gossypol also reduced parasite viability (IC50 = 6.43 ± 0.66 μM), though cytotoxicity was observed in mammalian cells. While the known promiscuity of gossypol precludes attributing these effects solely to EmcMDH inhibition, these findings hint at EmcMDH as a functionally relevant metabolic enzyme and a potential drug target, providing a foundation for further validation and development of selective cMDH-targeted therapies.

item.title: Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopic Characterization of Chitosan Extracted from Black Soldier Fly Pupa Shells
item.description:
Abstract
Chitosan is widely used as a matrix in metal nanoparticle-based surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates; however, its intrinsic spectral features may interfere with analyte identification. Conventional Raman spectroscopy of chitosan is further limited by strong fluorescence, resulting in scarce, reliable spectral data. In this study, chitosan extracted from Black Soldier Fly (BSF) (Hermetia illucens) pupa shells was characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, and silver nanoparticle-enhanced SERS. SERS measurements enabled the acquisition of well-resolved vibrational spectra of chitosan despite the strong fluorescence observed in conventional Raman measurements. Comparison with commercial chitosan and literature data allowed identification of characteristic spectral features associated with the chitosan molecular structure. The synthesized chitosan exhibited distinct structural and spectroscopic characteristics compared with the commercial material, including differences in relative crystallinity and characteristic FTIR and SERS spectral features. The results demonstrate that SERS is a suitable complementary spectroscopic approach for the characterization of chitosan and provides spectral information for the interpretation of chitosan-associated signals in SERS measurements.

item.title: A Comprehensive In Vitro and In Silico Study of Acteoside: Cytotoxicity, Molecular Interactions, and DFT Reactivity Profiles
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, the cytotoxic effects of acteoside were comparatively evaluated in four cancer cell lines (MiaPaCa-2, HL-60, A549, and MDA-MB-231). Based on the greater sensitivity observed in MiaPaCa-2 cells, molecular docking against the EGFR/HER2 tyrosine kinase domain was subsequently performed to investigate a potential molecular interaction relevant to the observed cytotoxic response in all four cell lines, acteoside reduced cell viability in a dose-dependent manner, with the lowest IC50 observed in MiaPaCa-2 cells (IC50 = 166.9 μM). Molecular docking analysis revealed a favorable binding affinity of acteoside toward the EGFR/HER2 tyrosine kinase domain, with a predicted binding energy of −8.9 kcal/mol. DFT calculations revealed solvent-dependent electronic properties, while frontier molecular orbital, molecular electrostatic potential (MEP), noncovalent interaction, and electron localization analyses identified electron-rich reactive regions and potential interaction sites within the acteoside molecule. Overall, acteoside exhibits varying levels of cytotoxic activity across the tested cell lines, and further studies are required to elucidate its mechanism of action.

item.title: Recovery and Separation of Rare Earth Elements and Iron from Columbite Hydrometallurgical Effluent
item.description:
Abstract
Rare earth elements exhibit unique physicochemical properties that justify their broad technological applications and rising global demand. Concerns about supply risks and resource scarcity have intensified the search for alternative supply routes and secondary sources. In this study, rare earth elements were recovered from an acidic effluent generated during the hydrometallurgical processing of columbite. Citric acid was used as a complexing agent to promote metal differentiation, and its effects on selective precipitation and solvent extraction were evaluated. Complexation with citric acid at a Fe:cit ratio of 1:1.5 and at pH 3 produced a precipitate with a rare earth-to-Fe ratio ten times higher than that of the initial solution. Subsequent solvent extraction with 10% v/v D2EHPA in kerosene recovered 92% of the remaining rare earth elements, yielding a separation factor of 27. The proposed process generated two streams enriched in rare earth elements.

item.title: Assessing Linear FAME-Property Relationships in Heterogeneous Biodiesel Databases: A Sequential Cross-Validated Subset-Selection Approach
item.description:
Abstract
Linear correlations based on fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) composition provide a transparent approach for estimating biodiesel properties, although their applicability to heterogeneous literature databases depends on the existence of a consistent composition-property structure. This work assesses linear relationships for density, kinematic viscosity, flash point, and lower and higher heating values using the normalized shares of palmitic, stearic, oleic, linoleic, and linolenic esters. A sequential nested leave-one-out procedure selects, at each stage, the observation whose exclusion maximizes the cross-validated performance of the remaining subset. The complete procedure is also applied to response-permuted, or Y-randomized, surrogate databases. The archived operating point is the first stage at which the fitted real trajectory reaches Rfit2 ≥ 0.60, while the real-versus-permuted differential Δ(k) compares the fitted linear compatibility of the actual FAME-property pairing with the mean fitted linear compatibility obtained after response randomization. Because sustained removal also raises the surrogate trajectories, the fitted R2 alone is not interpreted as evidence of a composition–property relation; the comparison relies on Δ(k). Exploratory data analysis first characterizes the original databases through target-property distributions, descriptive statistics, and literature-source and feedstock representation. This baseline is then extended by comparing the original and retained databases in terms of literature-source and dominant-FAME retention, target-property distributions, principal-component coverage, and Spearman rank-correlation structure, showing that the retained subsets largely preserve the main compositional characteristics of the original databases. Cook’s distance and Williams plots provide independent influence flags for a substantial, but incomplete, fraction of the selected observations, including response-inconsistent and high-leverage cases. Selected observations are interpreted as operationally incompatible with the five-FAME linear description at their respective selection stages; possible causes include influence, omitted descriptors, or nonlinear behavior. The combined statistical, representational, and physical evidence supports conditional linear correlations for kinematic viscosity, flash point, and higher heating value, in decreasing order of feasibility. In contrast, the selected density and lower-heating-value databases do not provide sufficient evidence for reliable linear correlations using the five-FAME representation. Semisynthetic manufactured databases show above-blind enrichment of planted response mismatches and generally reproducible coefficient recovery, with property-specific exceptions. The proposed framework therefore provides a systematic means of identifying and characterizing linear-compatible regimes within heterogeneous biodiesel property databases.

item.title: Engineering pH-Responsive trans-Ferulic Acid/κ-Carrageenan Beads for On-Demand Micronutrient Delivery in Plants
item.description:
Abstract
Micronutrient deficiencies in soils are a critical challenge in agriculture, particularly in acidic soil environments where nutrient availability is strongly limited by fixation, leaching, and altered metal speciation. These constraints contribute to inefficient nutrient uptake and reduced crop yields. Conventional micronutrient supplementation methods, such as bulk fertilizer application and foliar sprays, are often inefficient, environmentally harmful, and unsustainable, underscoring the need for smarter delivery systems tailored to soil pH conditions. In this study, we developed biodegradable, pH-responsive microbeads fabricated from κ-carrageenan (κ-CG), sulphated polysaccharide derrived from algal biomass and trans-ferulic acid (TFA), a naturally occurring phenolic antioxidant with radical-scavenging activity. The κ-carrageenan/TFA-based microbeads, designated as κ-TF-B, were synthesized through an eco-friendly process and optimized for size, morphology, and stability. Characterization confirmed the successful incorporation of the constituent functional groups, while swelling, degradation, and release studies demonstrated pH-responsive delivery of essential micronutrients under acidic conditions (pH 4.0), mimicking acidic soil environments. The optimized κ-TF-B microbeads exhibited enhanced swelling at acidic pH and sustained micronutrient release throughout the study period. In addition, the microbeads showed strong antioxidant activity, with a radical-scavenging efficiency of 93.4%, attributed to the presence of TFA. For plant applications, κ-TF-All, defined as the κ-TF-B microbead formulation loaded with all four essential micronutrients (Mn2+, Zn2+, Cu2+, and Fe2+), was evaluated in soil and plant growth assays. κ-TF-All improved micronutrient availability and promoted plant growth, resulting in larger leaf area and a 3.3-fold increase in chlorophyll content in Arabidopsis thaliana compared with the negative control, without observable phytotoxic effects. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of κ-TF-All microbeads as an eco-friendly and pH-responsive platform for sustainable micronutrient delivery and improved plant growth under micronutrient-limited conditions.

item.title: Introducing Chirality into Graphene Oxide Layers through a Facile Amino Acid-Based Covalent Functionalization
item.description:
Abstract
Graphene-based materials, including graphene oxide (GO), intrinsically lack stereocenters, limiting their usefulness in applications where chirality plays a crucial role. Covalent attachment of chiral molecules offers a promising strategy to introduce stereogenic elements into layers of GO. In this work, we report a one-pot method for the covalent functionalization of GO with lysine, exploiting the reactivity of the aminic groups of the amino acid toward epoxy groups located on the basal plane of the layers. Chirally functionalized layers of GO were prepared using d- and l-lysine and extensively purified to remove unreacted amino acid residuals. A comprehensive spectroscopic characterization confirms the successful functionalization, resulting in ∼3% N content. The chirality of the molecules bound to the resulting GO layers (relying on a rigorous purification by dialysis) was demonstrated through their interaction with a water-soluble porphyrin, which yielded chiral J-aggregates. The corresponding circular dichroism spectra confirmed that the porphyrin assemblies adopt distinct chiral configurations when templated by d- or l-GO. These findings highlight a straightforward route to impart chiral features to GO, expanding its applicability to several relevant fields, such as asymmetric catalysis, nanofiltration, and chiral sensing.

item.title: Polysiloxane-Coated Diamond Fillers for Enhanced Interfacial Compatibility in Epoxy Composites
item.description:
Abstract
This study aims to address the issues of poor interfacial compatibility, weak bonding strength, and difficult processing in diamond/epoxy composites through surface modification. Methyltrimethoxysilane (MTMS) was employed to construct a polysiloxane precursor on the surface of diamond microparticles with different particle sizes. Calcination was conducted to obtain modified diamond particles coated with amorphous SiO2 under different atmospheres and temperatures. The modified diamond particles were subsequently blended with epoxy resin. The effects of different amounts of MTMS addition and calcination conditions on the chemical structure and morphology of the coating layer, as well as on the rheological and thermal properties of the resulting composites, were systematically investigated. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) analyses confirmed the successful formation of the coating layer and its evolution with varying calcination conditions, XPS and solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (Solid-state NMR) reveal that the surface of diamond contains OH-terminated groups. Rheological tests demonstrated that surface coating significantly reduced the viscosity of the composites compared to uncoated samples. Rheological and thermal performance evaluations revealed that the composite filled with diamond particles modified with 2 wt % MTMS and calcined at 650 °C under a N2 atmosphere (Dia-0.7) exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a thermal conductivity of 0.65 W/m·K. This study provides an effective interface design strategy for the preparation of high-performance thermally conductive composites.

item.title: Effects of pH and MgSO 4 on Lignin Redeposition and Retention during Brownstock Washing
item.description:
Abstract
Process closure in kraft pulp mills requires increased recycling of washing liquors, which can alter liquor composition and promote lignin redeposition during brownstock washing. This study investigates the effect of pH and magnesium ions (Mg2+) on lignin retention and removal from pulp fibers in controlled washing experiments. Unbleached and bleached softwood kraft pulps were washed with industrial liquors collected from different stages of the kraft process at a Swedish mill. Lignin redeposition and retention were assessed using kappa number, brightness, and alkaline leaching. Within the alkaline pH range investigated, decreasing pH was generally associated with increased lignin retention on the fibers. NaOH addition improved lignin removal, but the effect plateaued beyond a liquor-dependent threshold. MgSO4 addition had little effect at the mill-relevant concentration of 1 g/L, whereas the deliberately elevated concentration of 10 g/L increased lignin retention. Overall, the results demonstrate that liquor chemistry influences the balance between lignin removal and retention during brownstock washing. Because conventional mill-scale indicators such as chemical oxygen demand (COD), dissolved solids carryover, and wash loss were not measured, the results are interpreted specifically in terms of lignin redeposition and retention rather than overall washer performance.

item.title: In Vivo Femtonewton-Sensing Nanotribology of Tradescantia Zebrina Leaf Cell Inner Surface Using Roll Rotation Detection
item.description:
Abstract
Accessing the properties of a plant cell interior noninvasively is difficult due to the presence of a cell wall. Nanoparticles larger than 5 nm cannot be readily phagocytosed inside the cell like animal cells. It is here that we realize that Tradescantia zebrina plant cells have prismatic forms of calcium oxalate crystals present inside them naturally. These crystals make a ready choice to study properties of the inner cell surface with the application of optical tweezers.
